13:20.race_name: Sky Bet Supreme Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Has a solid record (131211) for current yard and may rate higher still over hurdles
runners.name: Baron Noir
runners.owner: Noel Fehily Racing Syndicate- Baron Noir
runners.spotlight: Has built up a solid record (131211) for current yard and justified favouritism at Kempton (2m, good; third attempt over hurdles) most recently; acts on soft; ties in with Sober Glory and El Cairos on useful bumper form, although he looked rather fortunate to beat the latter (who might have won but for proving wayward) at Punchestown; his bare figures in this sphere fall short of Supreme standard but improvement remains possible.

runners.comment: 2-2 under front-running tactics, latest success in Thurles handicap; this is harder
runners.name: Eachtotheirown
runners.spotlight: Evidently well suited by being able to dominate as he's 2-2 under front-running tactics (0-3 otherwise); trounced his rivals in Thurles handicap (2m, yielding) most recently, proving well ahead of a mark of 124; should have more to offer in the right circumstances and grade but this scenario fails on both counts; faces a stiff task on the figures and competition for the lead.

runners.comment: Clumsy at the final flight in both hurdles attempts but has a big engine; shortlisted
runners.name: El Cairos
runners.spotlight: Appears to act on any ground; good fifth in the Champion Bumper at this meeting last year then might have won at Punchestown but for hanging badly left; sold for £410,000 at the David Maxwell dispersal in October; clumsy at the final flight in both attempts over hurdles, causing him to stumble and fall when looking the likely winner at Leopardstown but getting away with it and comfortably beating his rivals at Thurles (2m); not without his flaws but has a big engine and brings serious potential to this return to Cheltenham.

runners.comment: Useful and has Graded from but may lack the class needed for this assignment
runners.name: Koktail Brut
runners.spotlight: Proved useful in bumpers but is held by a couple of today's rivals on Punchestown festival running; form over hurdles (kept to 2m) features a narrow success in Grade 2 at Fairyhouse and respectable fourth in steadily run Grade 1 at Leopardstown, sandwiching a Christmas flop that is best forgiven (bled from nose); however, may lack the class needed for this assignment.

runners.comment: Prolific in French bumpers; won his latest hurdles start emphatically; keeps progressing
runners.name: Leader dAllier
runners.spotlight: Acts on any ground; prolific in French bumpers, bagging Grade 3 honours the final time; has started favourite in two maiden hurdles since joining Willie Mullins and made all for an emphatic success at Punchestown (2m) latest, building on his Leopardstown effort and taking overall record to 6-8; brings good qualities, being a very productive sort who keeps progressing.

runners.comment: Well bred; recorded a 38l success at Fairyhouse; highly regarded and hugely promising
runners.name: Mighty Park
runners.spotlight: Twice-raced 5yo who is highly regarded by his top trainer and looks a hugely exciting prospect, one with a Cheltenham Festival pedigree to boot (related to two winners at this meeting); recorded an effortless 38l success from the front in maiden hurdle at Fairyhouse (2m, soft) to build on the promise he showed in a point and, from the mouth of Willie Mullins, draw comparisons with Faugheen; an unexpected late switcher to this prize, having seemed more likely to run in the Turners; brings enormous potential and is a thoroughly fascinating contender, despite his inexperience.

runners.comment: Favourite for this race prior to a Formby defeat that can be excused; remains of interest
runners.name: Mydaddypaddy
runners.spotlight: Absent since being outgunned by Supreme absentee Idaho Sun when perhaps indirectly hindered by the low sun in Grade 1 at Aintree (2m1f, good to soft; four hurdles were omitted) on Boxing Day, losing his unbeaten record and his position at the head of the ante-post betting for this contest; gained his three wins in easy fashion, looking a very smart prospect, and may yet fulfil his potential; form is broadly solid; the likely frenetic pace here will suit this strong traveller who is ridden with hold-up tactics; remains of strong interest.

runners.comment: Impressive in Haydock Grade 2 last time, taking hurdles record to 3-3; top on ratings
runners.name: Old Park Star
runners.spotlight: Has made far more progress over hurdles than seemed likely, having been 0-3 (admittedly placed each time) in bumpers for Paul Nicholls; 3-3 in this sphere for new stable, winning by 12l at Cheltenham (2m1f) and 18l at Haydock (1m7f Grade 2) the last two occasions, both on good to soft ground; strong traveller who was particularly impressive from the front last time (he doesn't necessarily need to dominate); brother to a Cheltenham Festival winner; greatly respected in his bid to give Nicky Henderson a sixth success in this race.

runners.comment: Well held in Grade 2 when attempting to follow up his Wexford win; bottom on the figures
runners.name: Sageborough
runners.spotlight: Raced only twice (both over 2m) and may do better still but he's bottom of this pack on bare figures and needs his sights lowering; last of seven finishers in the Fairyhouse Grade 2 won by Koktail Brut when attempting to follow up a Wexford success that came at the chief expense of a rival who remains a longstanding maiden.

runners.comment: Beaten only once; impressive at Newbury last time; should make a bold bid from the front
runners.name: Sober Glory
runners.spotlight: Has seemed best over hurdles when making the running and met his sole defeat when those tactics weren't employed; impressively defied a big penalty at Newbury (2m, heavy) most recently, taking record in this sphere to 3-4 and overall strike-rate to 7-8, as well as achieving a very notable RPR; related to a Cheltenham Festival winner for his yard; worth his place at this level and should make a bold bid.

runners.breeder: E A R L De Faydeau
runners.comment: Smart; did well to get up in steadily run Grade 1 at the DRF; stronger pace here can help
runners.name: Talk The Talk
runners.spotlight: Should be unbeaten over hurdles as he looked the likely winner when final-flight faller in Grade 1 at Leopardstown (2m, yielding) over Christmas; gained compensation in same grade over the same C&D (heavy) at the Dublin Racing Pestival, taking record in this sphere to 3-4 and doing well to get up on the line having come from off the steady gallop set by the runner-up; he's called Talk The Talk but is certainly walking the walk too; major contender, especially with a stronger pace on the cards.

runners.comment: Quite useful on Flat and still unexposed over hurdles; may build on Punchestown maiden win
runners.name: Too Bossy For Us
runners.spotlight: Versatile as regards ground; quite a useful Flat handicapper; showed clear promise with midfield finish in the Triumph at this meeting 12 months ago on the first of his three attempts over hurdles; most recently recorded a comfortable success, with tongue-tie applied, in a Punchestown maiden (2m) that his connections' Ethical Diamond won last year en route to a good effort at the Cheltenham Festival and a prestigious Flat treble; could go well.

14:00.race_name: Singer Arkle Challenge Trophy Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Sole chase win came in an uncompetitive race; bottom of the list on ratings
runners.name: Hansard
runners.spotlight: Had a simple task when beating two stablemates at Lingfield (2m, good to soft) in December; finished behind Jax Junior and Mambonumberfive in his runs on either side of that win; bottom of the list on ratings.

runners.comment: Fine start to chasing career (3-5); improvement needed but straightforward and jumps well
runners.name: Jax Junior
runners.spotlight: Bled from nose when well held behind Steel Ally at Ascot just before Christmas but otherwise he's made a fine start to his chasing career, winning a handicap at Sandown (1m7f, soft) and Grade 2 novice at Kempton (2m4f, good to soft) on last two starts; needs a chunk of improvement to trouble the principals but he's straightforward, tactically versatile and a sound jumper.

runners.breeder: Earl Les Bordes De Mornay & G Hanquiez
runners.comment: Last year's Supreme winner; 1-1 over fences; the one to beat with a clear round
runners.name: Kopek Des Bordes
runners.spotlight: Travelled strongly when landing the odds in last year's Supreme (good to soft) before running no sort of race at Punchestown; dispatched inferior opposition with minimum of fuss on debut over fences at Navan (2m1f, soft/heavy) in November; hasn't been seen since (had a loose chip removed from a knee in December) and lacks the chasing experience of his rivals, but he certainly possesses the X factor and he's the one to beat with a clear round.

runners.comment: Unbeaten in chases; follows same path as stablemates Sprinter Sacre and Altior; big chance
runners.name: Lulamba
runners.spotlight: Leading juvenile hurdler last season, following narrow defeat in the Triumph with clearcut success at Punchestown, and he is 3-3 over fences; easily landed the odds in Grade 1 novice at Sandown (1m7f, good to soft) in December and he readily beat five older rivals in Grade 2 Game Spirit at Newbury (2m, heavy) last month; stellar stablemates Sprinter Sacre and Altior followed the Game Spirit path to Arkle success, and he's a very strong candidate.

runners.comment: Completed hat-trick towards end of 2025; ran poorly on heavy going last time; lots to find
runners.name: Mambonumberfive
runners.spotlight: On a roll towards the end of 2025, completing a hat-trick of chase wins in Grade 2 novice at Kempton (2m, good; beat Hansard by 7l) just after Christmas; possibly unsuited by heavy ground when a well-beaten last of three behind Steel Ally at Warwick next time, jumping poorly; should encounter less testing conditions here but has plenty to find on the figures.

runners.comment: Made it 3-3 over fences with Warwick win; progressive but will need another personal best
runners.name: Steel Ally
runners.spotlight: Pulled up on two of his last three goes over hurdles but the transition to chasing has been smooth and he's 3-3; showed further improvement when easily beating two rivals (Mambonumberfive well held in third) in Grade 2 Kingmaker Novices' at Warwick (2m, heavy; handles good) last month; faces his sternest assignment and will need another personal best.

runners.comment: 2025 County Hurdle winner; just lost out in Irish Arkle after titanic tussle; respected
runners.name: Kargese
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in the 2024 Triumph Hurdle and won last year's County; has quickly reached a similar level over fences, winning a beginners' event at Leopardstown (2m1f, yielding) just after Christmas and going down to the high-class Romeo Coolio in Grade 1 over the same C&D (soft) only after a titanic tussle and a final-fence blunder; should be in the thick of things again if fully recovered from those exertions.

14:40.race_name: McCoy Contractors Juvenile Handicap Hurdle (Premier Handicap) (Registered As The Fred Winter) (GBB)

runners.breeder: E A R L Elevage De Pierrepont
runners.comment: Maiden winner who cut little ice in a Grade 1 last time; doesn't look a Mullins masterplan
runners.name: Bertutea
runners.spotlight: AW winner; turf form on very soft or heavy; badly in with The Mighty Celt on their French clash; it was all very straightforward on his Irish debut at Limerick but he cut little ice in a Grade 1 at the Dublin Racing Festival (18-1); doesn't look a Mullins masterplan and the yard is 0-25 in this race; tongue-tie added.

runners.comment: Won hurdles debut but reality checks have followed at Graded level
runners.name: Barbizon
runners.spotlight: One of two runners for a yard that's won this four times; ran to a smart level on the Flat and made a winning start over hurdles, but reality checks have followed in Graded races won by tip-top juvenile Narciso Has; hardly brings momentum into his handicap debut and has a lot of weight; there will be no ground excuses.

runners.comment: Comfortable maiden winner last time and it's hard to identify the ceiling of his ability
runners.name: Madness dElle
runners.spotlight: Has raced on only soft or heavy ground; progressive form figures and he looked full of beans when accounting for a respected rival with the pair dominant in a maiden at Gowran Park last month; he dictated up front in that slowly run race, so the bare form is perhaps best treated with an element of caution; however, he runs in this instead of the Triumph and it's hard to identify the ceiling of his ability.

runners.comment: Likely contender for all that the handicapper has factored potential into his initial mark
runners.name: Harwa
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in both his French races and he comfortably reeled in the front-runners to justify market confidence (100-30) on his Irish debut at Fairyhouse (heavy); good to soft ground would be a first but he might well approve of drier conditions as he's not the biggest; trainer's form figures in this race are 146P and there were excuses for the one who pulled up; respected, for all that the handicapper has factored potential into this initial mark.

runners.comment: Made hay on good ground last summer; excused French run on heavy going last time
runners.name: Dignam
runners.spotlight: When all his best form on the Flat and over hurdles is on good ground, it's best to put a line through his run on heavy in a French Grade 1 last time (November); he beat little of note when making hay in minor jumps meetings last summer but barely broke sweat in any of those races and his jumping was pinpoint accurate; one to be interested in for a trainer (also runs Glen To Glen) who knows what's required for this; gelded since his last run.

runners.comment: Eyecatching third to Manlaga on British debut; could easily improve on that form
runners.name: The Mighty Celt
runners.spotlight: His French form fills the eye and the experience of six races there will stand him in good stead; underwent wind and gelding operations prior to his debut for Dan Skelton and, with a hood added to regular tongue-tie, he ran on promisingly for third behind Manlaga at Haydock a month ago (soft); it's easy to envisage him finding a fair bit on that form; has raced only on ground ranging from soft to heavy.

runners.comment: Made all at Ascot latest; respected, for all that front-running spells danger in this race
runners.name: Winston Junior
runners.owner: R Bartlett J Carthy & Mrs P Shanahan
runners.spotlight: Has more scope than your typical ex-Flat 4yo and he was a useful maiden in that scene at up to 1m5f; came up short in his first two hurdle races but was unlucky not to be closer to leading Triumph contender Minella Study here in December (good to soft) and then, despite racing freely, won as he liked when a strong favourite at Ascot (soft); made all that day and those tactics can spell danger in a race of this nature, but he should have more to give; Jack Kennedy is a notable booking with the Elliott stable represented.

runners.comment: Impressive in how she took care of Pourquoi Pas Papa at Haydock; dangerously unexposed
runners.name: Manlaga
runners.spotlight: Won her sole French start, on heavy; both British runs on soft, coming up shy in a Listed race after 315 days off but stylish in quickening away from Pourquoi Pas Papa at Haydock a month ago; could have run in the Triumph but rocks up here with a dangerously unexposed profile.

runners.breeder: Lynch Bages Ltd & Camas Park Stud
runners.comment: Smart Flat horse; improved second at Naas in a race that's been a good guide to this
runners.name: Saratoga
runners.spotlight: Six Flat runs for Aidan O'Brien, best form at 1m6f/2m; jumping was ropey in his first two defeats over hurdles but that part of his game improved when a rallying second in a rated hurdle at Naas (soft to heavy) that has delivered four of the last seven winners of this race; probably peaking at the right time when this has all the hallmarks of a long-term plan; seems versatile ground-wise; lots to like.

runners.comment: Had a break since his maiden win at Cork and stable knows what's required in this race
runners.name: Glen To Glen
runners.spotlight: Won his Flat maiden over 6f but stayed 1m2f; had no problem staying 2m over hurdles when showing significant improvement to win at Cork in early December, keeping on willingly to thwart solid yardstick Ole Ole; it's probably safe to turn a blind eye to his subsequent absence when his trainer has won three of the last seven runnings of this race; there has been money about for him in the last fortnight; Flat profile suggests he may benefit from today's surface (all hurdle runs in the mud).

runners.comment: Third in a Grade 2 only 17 days ago and appeals as one with better days ahead of him
runners.name: Mustang Du Breuil
runners.spotlight: Ran only 17 days ago when relinquishing his unbeaten record at the hands of older opposition in the Grade 2 Dovecote at Kempton (good to soft); Nicky Henderson was forced into that commitment to register the requisite third run to qualify here and that defeat was no backward step; light on experience with no Flat background but, like so many in here, he no doubt has better days ahead of him; James Bowen has been aboard for his two British runs.

runners.comment: Second to Manlaga at Haydock; 6lb better off with that rival here
runners.name: Pourquoi Pas Papa
runners.spotlight: Advanced his form when doing it comfortably at Wincanton (1m7f, heavy) and again in chasing home Manlaga at Haydock (1m7f, soft); couldn't live with the winner (with whom he's 6lb better off) late on but being pestered up front didn't help the cause and he's open to further improvement in a race of this nature on handicap debut; Paul Nicholls has won three of these with recruits from France, where this horse was second last summer.

runners.comment: Leopardstown maiden winner; had excuses when 4-1 for a Grade 2 here on Trials Day
runners.name: Hardy Stuff
runners.spotlight: Hooded since looking tricky on his debut; the ground was yielding when he displayed a good turn of foot to edge out Ole Ole in a Leopardstown maiden over Christmas and he was too free for his own good when strong in the betting for a Grade 2 here on Trials Day (soft); a combination of the expected good to soft ground and a bigger-field scenario heightens interest in this Flat bred; needs a close look.

runners.comment: Dual hurdle winner and beaten by a Triumph contender last time; had recent AW run
runners.name: Ammes
runners.spotlight: Good Flat horse before embarking on hurdling career and his odds-on defeat to Triumph contender Minella Study at Wetherby in October (Listed; good) doesn't look too shoddy now given the winner's subsequent exploits; appears to have been saved for this since and last month's run on the AW (sixth) should have cleared the pipes; good ground seems his preference but effective on good to soft.

runners.comment: Form has gone backwards since he looked good at Sandown in December
runners.name: Macktoad
runners.spotlight: French bumper winner who created a huge impression on his British debut when unextended at Sandown in December (soft) but his reputation has taken a severe knock after heavy defeats at Chepstow (good to soft) and Haydock (soft; in cheekpieces but not now); his jumping was shoddy on his penultimate run and it's ominous that connections blamed the ground last time, opining that it was drying out; opposable on a few counts.

runners.comment: Beginning to look a shade exposed and that never bodes well in this race
runners.name: Ole Ole
runners.spotlight: Beaten four times but significant promise in all of those runs (the first in France), finishing second to Quinta Do Lago, Glen To Glen and Hardy Stuff in his respective Irish maidens; seemed to appreciate the yielding ground last time at Leopardstown (previous runs were in the mud) but he is beginning to look a shade exposed and that never bodes well in this race.

runners.comment: Well held on last two runs but behind smart opposition; Irish trainer always respected
runners.name: Quinta Do Lago
runners.spotlight: This dual winner (on good/soft to heavy) has had his limitations laid bare the last twice, though they were classy juveniles he bumped into last time at Fairyhouse and that was probably his best performance (he didn't look out of his comfort zone deep into the race); legendary Irish trainer Jessica Harrington rarely brings one over without a degree of optimism; cheekpieces added.

runners.comment: Flat/hurdle winner in France; this could be a culture shock on his British/handicap debut
runners.name: Paddockwood
runners.spotlight: Won only one of his 15 Flat races in France but won two of his four hurdle starts at Cagnes-Sur-Mer, both on very soft; this could be some culture shock on his British/handicap hurdle debut and it's worth bearing in mind that stablemate Bad had a similar profile when well beaten in this three years ago at odds of only 5-1.

runners.comment: Dual hurdle winner but beaten in the tougher assignments he's faced; vulnerable
runners.name: Klycot
runners.spotlight: French Flat winner who has won two of his four races over hurdles but was beaten about 7l in the tougher assignments he's faced; in fairness, his Wetherby win in January (2m, soft) was another step in the right direction but he's probably placed if he's lucky.

runners.comment: Picked up a penalty for his win at Sandown on Saturday; did that comfortably
runners.name: Bibe Mus
runners.spotlight: 1m2f French Flat winner; won a maiden hurdle (yielding) in Ireland in October and continued his progress with seconds this winter in a Listed race and Punchestown handicap; even better when winning comfortably on his stable debut at Sandown on Saturday (soft), picking up the penalty that secured his place here; connections strike while the iron is hot and he merits attention, for all that Harry Cobden was aboard at the weekend but not now.

runners.comment: Ex-French; might be on a tough mark and can find his level further down the line
runners.name: Bandjo
runners.spotlight: Won his only Flat start in France (1m4f, good to soft) and later added a hurdles win on very soft ground at Cagnes-Sur-Mer; French recruits often kick off in Britain with tough marks before finding their level further down the line; reservations.

runners.breeder: E A R L Ecurie Des Mottes
runners.comment: French bumper winner; 0-3 over hurdles and already needs further by the looks of it
runners.name: Mino Des Mottes
runners.spotlight: French bumper winner on good to soft; his maiden form is nothing to go wild about, though he did at least run better when second to a shorter-priced stablemate at Punchestown last month (soft to heavy); already needs further by the looks of it.

15:20.race_name: Trustmarque Ultima Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Won hot, 3-runner graduation chase at Ascot in December; entitled to considerable respect
runners.name: Iroko
runners.spotlight: Fourth in last season's Grand National (4m2f, good to soft) off 5lb lower; the big one at Aintree is again his main target but this 8yo looked better than ever when winning a hot, three-runner graduation chase at Ascot (2m5f, good to soft) in December and on that evidence he's entitled to considerable respect off his revised mark; won the Martin Pipe Hurdle at the 2023 Festival.

runners.comment: 2m4f Grade 1 novice chase win last February; needs something extra on this season's form
runners.name: Handstands
runners.spotlight: 2m4f Grade 1 novice chase winner last February; a couple of good runs in defeat this term, last time third of five at Windsor (2m6f, soft; first run after wind surgery), but he needs something extra today and there's a suspicion a shorter trip may be preferable; well beaten (over hurdles) on sole run here; cheekpieces go on.

runners.comment: Won bet365 Gold Cup last April; each-way shout if minimising the mistakes; headgear change
runners.name: Resplendent Grey
runners.spotlight: Won the bet365 Gold Cup at Sandown (extended 3m4f, good) last April in first-time cheekpieces and returned to form when second at Windsor (2m6f, soft) in January; his jumping can sometimes lack fluency but, with first-time blinkers replacing the cheekpieces, he has an each-way chance if minimising the mistakes; fourth of 18 in the NH Chase here (3m6f, good to soft) last March.

runners.comment: Won the 2m4f Plate here 12 months ago; this new trip could prompt further improvement
runners.name: Jagwar
runners.spotlight: Highly progressive switched to fences last season, a campaign that culminated in a convincing win in the Plate here (2m4f, good to soft) in March; he's kept on well over 2m4f here (good to soft/soft) on both runs this season, beaten just a head last time when 10l clear of the third; today's first crack at a staying trip could prompt further improvement; lots to like.

runners.comment: Won in good style here in December and the ground was heavy when well beaten next time
runners.name: Blaze The Way
runners.owner: Molly Willis & Paul Willis & Brian Groarke & Tom Groarke
runners.spotlight: Off the mark over fences at fifth attempt in good style here (3m2f, good to soft) in December, when back up in trip; well beaten in Grade 3 novice at Naas since but the heavy ground provides an excuse; a mark 8lb higher than for his course win may not be insurmountable for this unexposed 8yo.

runners.breeder: Jean-Pierre Dubois & Scea Haras Du Ma
runners.comment: Not disgraced in Grade 2 at Newbury latest; not ruled out each-way now back in a handicap
runners.name: Leave Of Absence
runners.spotlight: Second-season chaser who is enjoying another progressive campaign, winning a novice here (3m1f, good) in October and beaten a head in a handicap at Ascot (3m, good to soft) in December; not disgraced in Grade 2 at Newbury (2m7f, heavy) last time; not ruled out each-way now back in a handicap.

runners.comment: Below best at Haydock but wind op since and he went very close in last season's Kim Muir
runners.name: Johnnywho
runners.spotlight: Neck second in the Kim Muir here (3m2f, good to soft) 12 months ago; promise in defeat on his first two runs this season; not quite at the top of his game at Haydock last time but wind op since and cheekpieces are added; remains one to be interested in, especially given his Festival form.

runners.comment: Thrived towards end of 2025; good third most recently; further improvement not ruled out
runners.name: Konfusion
runners.spotlight: 8yo who thrived towards the end of last year, winning three times (2m7f/3m, good-soft); having gone up the weights he was third of six (beaten about 2l) behind Imperial Saint at Haydock (3m1f, good to soft) in January but that was still a big performance and further improvement can't be ruled out.

runners.comment: Below par last time but each-way claims on earlier form, provided he finds some fluency
runners.name: Search For Glory
runners.spotlight: Didn't jump well when seventh in this last year and pulled up in the Thyestes at Gowran Park (3m1f, heavy) in January on latest run; however, he was in good form previously, finishing second of nine at Navan (2m4f, soft to heavy) then second of 28 in the Paddy Power Chase at Leopardstown (3m, yielding); each-way player if back on song and finding some fluency.

runners.comment: Course winner who is well treated on his form in 2023 but this 11yo has struggled since
runners.name: Stolen Silver
runners.spotlight: Course winner who is well handicapped on his form in 2023 but this 11yo has struggled since; tailed off on stable debut at Kelso ten days ago.

runners.comment: Won over 3m1f at Haydock in January and unexposed over staying distances; could go well
runners.name: Imperial Saint
runners.spotlight: Progressive novice last season, winning three handicaps at Aintree (2m/2m4f, good/good to soft) and posting a good third here (2m4f, soft); won at Haydock (3m1f, good to soft) in January when back up in trip and he's unexposed over staying distances; up 3lb for that neck victory; could go well.

runners.comment: Kept on for close second over 2m4f recently; the step back up in trip could be a firm plus
runners.name: Blow Your Wad
runners.spotlight: Kept on well for third in handicap at Ascot (3m, good) in November and creditable third of six on stable debut in Grade 1 Ascot Chase (2m5f, good to soft) last month, before close second in handicap at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft) ten days ago; he was 10l clear of the third last time and is 4lb ahead of the handicapper off the same mark today; the step back up in trip could be a firm plus and he showed promise here last April; one to consider seriously.

runners.comment: 3-5 here and close fourth at Ascot in December when last seen; could be in the mix
runners.name: Hyland
runners.spotlight: Won Listed novice chase here (3m, good) in November 2024; 0-5 in handicaps in 2025 but having edged down the weights he was a close fourth at Ascot (3m, good to soft) in December last time; 3-5 here and, with the drying ground in his favour, he could be in the mix in first-time cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Return to form needed but it's hard to forget his dominant display in this 12 months ago
runners.name: Myretown
runners.spotlight: Mistakes were costly on first two runs this term and he was pulled up at Haydock (extended 3m4f, good to soft) 24 days ago; not easy to fancy on the back of that but stamina may well have been an issue and he was hugely impressive when making all by 11l in this race last March (good to soft); might take plenty of catching, even now 15lb higher, if rediscovering that same dominant form.

runners.comment: Two big runs at Kempton this year but he may prove vulnerable up the Cheltenham hill
runners.name: The Doyen Chief
runners.spotlight: Won at Kempton (3m, good) in January and good second in competitive handicap there (3m, good to soft) last month; could give another good account but he didn't quite stay when fifth here (extended 3m2f, good to soft) in December and it's possible he'll again prove vulnerable up the hill.

runners.comment: Best performance over hurdles came at 3m; possible improver now back up in trip
runners.name: Quebecois
runners.spotlight: Mixed form during this novice chase campaign but he went very close in handicap here (2m4f, soft) in January and 2m was against him back in novice company at Newbury latest; best performance over hurdles came when winning at 3m at Ayr (good to soft) last April; possible improver now back up in trip.

runners.comment: Twice made the frame here towards the end of last year and he's an each-way candidate
runners.name: The Short Go
runners.spotlight: Didn't jump well when 16l fifth to Myretown in this race last March (good to soft); solid course record otherwise and he twice made the frame here (3m1f/3m2f, good/good to soft) towards the end of last year; has had a wind operation since and he's an each-way candidate if jumping better than 12 months ago.

runners.breeder: Brittas House Stud And Grenane House
runners.comment: 7yo who is lightly raced over fences and from a top Irish yard but needs to raise his game
runners.name: Patter Merchant
runners.spotlight: 7yo who is lightly raced over fences and represents top Irish yard; went close at Fairyhouse in November on second chase start but his form has gone the wrong way since and he was soundly beaten at Punchestown last month in his first handicap chase; ninth in the Pertemps Final here last March.

runners.comment: Stamina untested but form of latest, easy win in veterans' chase is working out very well
runners.name: Filanderer
runners.spotlight: 10yo who is lightly raced for his age and made it five wins from his last six starts (various ground) when scoring comfortably in a veterans' chase at Market Rasen in January (extended 2m5f; the longest trip he's tackled); this is a hot race in which to test his stamina, and from out of the handicap he's 11lb higher than last time, but he was strong at the finish and the form is working out very well; it remains to be seen where his limitations lie.

runners.comment: 4lb wrong but this unexposed 6yo has been showing promise and is not ruled out each-way
runners.name: Knight Of Allen
runners.spotlight: Kept on for creditable fourth of five in novice chase here (2m4f, good) in January when up against it at the weights and he may have bumped into a handicap blot when 14l second at Newbury (extended 2m7f, heavy) last month; this unexposed 6yo is not ruled out each-way, despite being 4lb wrong.

runners.breeder: M Richard Venn Bloodstock Ltd & M J W
runners.comment: Second at Bangor in November on reappearance but two underwhelming runs have followed
runners.name: Margarets Legacy
runners.spotlight: Won last winter on first two starts for yard (2m4f, good to soft/soft) and looked set for another progressive season when second at Bangor (2m4f, soft) on reappearance; however, two underwhelming runs have followed.

runners.comment: 3 wins last season; didn't run badly at Ascot last time but 9lb out of the handicap today
runners.name: Eyed
runners.spotlight: 9yo who was progressive last season, winning three times (2m5f/3m, good/good to soft); he didn't run badly when fifth at Ascot (3m, soft) in January last time but is 9lb out of the handicap today, so faces a tough task.

16:00.race_name: Unibet Champion Hurdle Challenge Trophy (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Impressive in major handicap over C&D in November; won the Kingwell last time; progressive
runners.name: Alexei
runners.spotlight: Acts on any ground; impressive in major handicap over C&D in November; made harder work of justifying favouritism in the Kingwell (1m7f Grade 2) at Wincanton most recently, wandering under pressure to boot, and this is a stiffer assignment, but he's a broadly progressive contender who is 5-9 over hurdles and may rate higher still; possibilities in a year where some big names have dropped out.

runners.comment: Has lost his unbeaten record since upped to Grade 1 level but a bigger effort is possible
runners.name: Anzadam
runners.spotlight: Looked very promising in completing a Grade 3 double in great style upon joining Willie Mullins; has lost his unbeaten record since upped to Grade 1 level, beaten by Golden Ace in the Fighting Fifth then only fourth twice at Leopardstown (headstrong on penultimate start); however, this first taste of the Cheltenham Festival may facilitate a bigger effort, with the possibility of an ideal pace set-up and precise priming for this day.

runners.comment: Landed the Triumph last year on hurdles debut; open to further improvement back here
runners.name: Poniros
runners.spotlight: Belied his 100-1 odds with a remarkable success in the Triumph at this meeting (2m1f, good to soft) last year on hurdles debut, collaring Lulamba who subsequently reversed placings with him at Punchestown and is a leading contender in today's Arkle; ran below expectations at Royal Ascot but ran promisingly, with a view to this race, in the Irish Champion Hurdle on return from layoff (got detached in the back straight, ending up with plenty to do, then stayed on for third of five); could be open to plenty of further improvement with that outing under his belt and given his very low mileage in this sphere; very interesting back at Cheltenham.

runners.breeder: R D & Mrs J S Chugg
runners.comment: Won the Turners last year and Cheltenham Grade 2 latest start; unbeaten in completed runs
runners.name: The New Lion
runners.spotlight: Bids to emulate Istabraq, Hardy Eustace and Faugheen by winning the Champion Hurdle a year after landing the 2m5f Grade 1 novice hurdle at this meeting; held a 1l lead, still not under maximum pressure, when falling two out in the Fighting Fifth on reappearance; unbeaten otherwise and is better than the bare form he showed in a Grade 2 at Cheltenham (2m1f, soft) last time when the steady pace wasn't conducive to an ideal test; still has plenty of potential in open company and commands respect, especially with a stronger gallop seemingly on the cards.

runners.breeder: E A R L Elevage Figerro & Hubert Favre
runners.comment: Improving; thoroughly dominant off top weight in major handicap at Newbury last time
runners.name: Tutti Quanti
runners.spotlight: Never-dangerous sixth in the Supreme on this card 12 months ago but ran well on bare figures despite a big change in tactics (normally leads or races prominently); took his strike-rate to 4-9 with wins in notable handicaps at Newbury (2m, soft/heavy) in November and February, last time defying top weight and proving thoroughly dominant in the race that fellow front-runner Make A Stand won in 1997 before following up in the Champion Hurdle; improving hurdler who is worth a crack at this prize in a reasonably open year and has been duly supplemented at a cost of £18,000

runners.comment: Grade 3 runner-up last time; faces stiffer task and competition for the lead in this field
runners.name: Workahead
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 8yo; dropped away from the top of the hill in the Supreme on this card 12 months ago, having raced freely and done too much up front; achieved best RPRs when scoring impressively at Leopardstown (strong maiden form) in December 2024 and good second in Grade 3 at Gowran Park (again over 2m; heavy) last time; faces a stiffer assignment and competition for the lead.

runners.comment: Leading player provided the form of her Irish Champion win is transferred to Cheltenham
runners.name: Brighterdaysahead
runners.spotlight: Has form on most types of ground; hasn't lived up to expectations at this meeting for the last two years, beaten by Golden Ace in the Grade 2 novice hurdle in 2024 and only fourth (weakening when hampered) in this contest in 2025; otherwise a very smart mare and produced one of her best performances in the Irish Champion Hurdle at Leopardstown (2m, heavy) most recently, reversing December placings with Lossiemouth and registering a fourth Grade 1 success; leading contender, provided she transfers the form to this venue.

runners.comment: Fortuitous winner of this race last year; may require further luck to retain her crown
runners.name: Golden Ace
runners.spotlight: Record of 3-4 at Cheltenham features two Festival wins, beating Brighterdaysahead in the Grade 2 novice hurdle in 2024 then admittedly fortuitous (left in lead when State Man took a late fall; odds-on Constitution Hill exited earlier) when 25-1 in this race last year; also had fortune on her side in this season's Fighting Fifth as the front two in the market, including The New Lion, failed to complete; ran creditably on Boxing Day when last seen; largely consistent and should go well but may require further luck to retain her crown.

runners.breeder: Sarl Elevage Des Vallons & M Ian Kellit
runners.comment: Prolific and very talented mare; record of 4-4 at Cheltenham includes three Festival wins
runners.name: Lossiemouth
runners.spotlight: Versatile as regards ground; prolific and highly talented mare whose record of 13-17 features nine Grade 1 wins, including three at this meeting (Triumph and two Mares' Hurdles); 4-4 at this venue overall; failed to justify favouritism in the Irish Champion Hurdle most recently but ran creditably without managing to confirm December placings with Brighterdaysahead; has less to prove than that rival back at Cheltenham and holds a big chance at the weights; wears headgear for the first time.

16:40.race_name: Sun Racing Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: S C E A Haras De La Perelle
runners.comment: Well held here last March; improved at 2m5f this winter but more needed than latest 4th
runners.name: Dee Capo
runners.spotlight: Nearer last than first in the novice handicap chase (extended 2m4f) at the Cheltenham Festival last March but he's a better horse now, having won at Punchestown (about 2m5f, soft to heavy) in November and been close up in a big field at Leopardstown under similar conditions last month; even more needed and he might prefer slower ground than is likely today; yard runs two.

runners.comment: Has impressed in two chase wins (2m1f and 2m4f) and best days still to come; respected
runners.name: Down Memory Lane
runners.spotlight: His campaigns can be short and not always sweet but he's had some excuses since making a sparkling chase debut at Navan (2m1f, yielding) in late 2024, including when returning with some mucus in a nostril in the Galway Plate last July; right back on his game when confidently ridden to win at Navan (about 2m4f, soft to heavy) in December, despite suffering some interference, and his best days could still lie ahead.

runners.comment: Hurdle wins at up to 2m1f;  2-4 over fences (2m3f/2m); this stiff finish asks a question
runners.name: No Questions Asked
runners.spotlight: Three hurdle wins at up to 2m1f last season but he was the last to finish in the Martin Pipe here (about 2m4f) last March; has proved his worth in small-field chases since, winning two from four starts, over 2m3f (good) and 2m (soft); he can raise his game further but a strongly run race on a track with a steep uphill finish raises a question.

runners.comment: Talented but delicate; soundly beaten and pulled up in his two runs for this yard
runners.name: Jungle Boogie
runners.spotlight: Talented but delicate 12yo who has run just ten times over the years; conditions suit but he's been soundly beaten and pulled up in his two starts for new yard; will do very well to add to trainer's three wins in the race.

runners.comment: Has hurdle form here but 2-15 over fences and races mostly on sharp tracks; up against it
runners.name: Boombawn
runners.spotlight: Has hurdle form at Cheltenham over a similar trip to today's but he races mostly on sharp tracks, albeit with soft ground against him in January when well back in his sole chase start here; never showed with a chance when upped to 3m at Kempton recently and he's no strong option to improve a 2-15 strike-rate over fences; yard runs two others with better claims.

runners.comment: Won 2-4 over fences and had no realistic chance in a Grade 1 latest; scope to do better
runners.name: Downmexicoway
runners.spotlight: Irish point winner; has won two of his four chase starts (at 2m/2m1f on good to yielding and heavy) and had no realistic chance in a Grade 1 at Leopardstown last month, but he could have made a better impression with some of his jumping; this is a new test for him under rules but he should have the scope to do better back in a handicap; yard runs three.

runners.comment: 0-10 in chases but two cracking runs here (about 2m4f) last spring; a possible reviver
runners.name: OMoore Park
runners.spotlight: Winless after ten chase starts but he ran two cracking races at about 2m4f on the New course here (good to soft and good) last spring off much the same mark as today's; has more to prove on this season's form but he has revival potential now back on less testing ground than last time and returned to a course that suits.

runners.breeder: Little Lodge Farm & Mr & Mrs Twr Chugg
runners.comment: Acts well here but on highest-ever chase mark following a Warwick win last month
runners.name: Guard Your Dreams
runners.spotlight: Fell in the Ultima last March but he has often run creditably over fences here and handles most surfaces; however, he's on his highest-ever chase mark following a Warwick win (about 2m4f, heavy) last month and now looks up against it.

runners.breeder: Sas Ecurie De Cachene & Elise Drouet
runners.comment: Has strong 2m4f course form off this mark; retains ability since absence; rock-solid
runners.name: Madara
runners.spotlight: Four chase wins for other yards, most recently in February 2024; 0-4 for this trainer but he achieved a lifetime best when close up on the New course (about 2m4f, good to soft) in December 2024, off this mark to an improver; has a strong record in other races here and looks to retain all his ability since back from an absence; regular cheekpieces refitted; rock-solid contender.

runners.comment: Improved show with 2m6f win at Newbury; up 9lb and lesser run since; might do better here
runners.name: Booster Bob
runners.spotlight: Has a useful jumps strike-rate and a Newbury chase win (about 2m6f, good to soft) in November showed he was still improving; a 9lb rise appeared beyond him on the New course since but he travelled strongly for a long way and may yet show he hasn't exhausted the handicapping options.

runners.comment: Lots of ability and has strong course form; soundly beaten, then fell, in 2 runs for yard
runners.name: Peaky Boy
runners.spotlight: Sparingly raced but has a lot of ability, making a successful chase debut over C&D (good) in November 2024 then close up in a well-contested handicap here (about 3m1f, good to soft); however, he didn't jump well when tailed off for new yard at Ascot last February and took a heavy early fall at Newcastle last month on his only start since; now goes in cheekpieces; talented but risky.

runners.comment: Ran well in 3m Pertemps hurdle last March; solid chase form at 2m2f-3m since; tongue tied
runners.name: Will The Wise
runners.spotlight: Improved spell over hurdles last spring included a sixth in the 3m Pertemps here; had a good experience when making all in a Galway chase (about 2m2f, yielding) in October and he's run well in two competitive staying handicaps since; needs improvement off this mark for the return to 2m4f but this test is worth investigating; tongue tied first time; thereabouts.

runners.comment: Has run some of his better races here, including 2m4f win last April; struggling of late
runners.name: Riskintheground
runners.spotlight: He's run some of his better races at Cheltenham, including a New course win (about 2m4f, good; off this mark) from O'Moore Park last April; not much going for him on his form since beating three rivals at Newton Abbot in October but some sort of revival isn't beyond the imagination.

runners.comment: Close 3rd in Grand Annual (2m) last year; well held since but some late support for him
runners.name: Midnight It Is
runners.spotlight: Hurdle winner at 2m3f; rarely ventures beyond 2m1f now and has something to prove in trying to repeat a very good third in the Grand Annual here (2m, good to soft; off 1lb lower) last March, having run three moderate races since, but there has been late support for him.

runners.comment: Progressive since back from a break; 9lb higher than for October win but may improve again
runners.name: Zurich
runners.spotlight: Humdrum start to chase career but a better horse since back from a break, following a Killarney win with an uncomplicated display over C&D (good) in October; would have finished closer than his near-4l third at Doncaster (2m3f, good to soft) in December but for a mistake at the last and that form has worked out; now 9lb higher than the latest win but open to improvement.

runners.comment: Good 2m6f win at Leicester but held off 8lb higher at Ascot since; this race looks tough
runners.name: Jipcot
runners.spotlight: Four hurdle wins; made just a so-so stab at chasing in late 2023 but he was footsure when making all at Leicester (about 2m6f, good to soft) in January and perhaps the 3m trip counted against him when trying to justify an 8lb rise at Ascot since; should have more to come over fences at some stage but this looks a tough call; yard also runs Peaky Boy.

runners.comment: Won valuable handicap hurdle last February; has chase potential and this trip should suit
runners.name: McLaurey
runners.spotlight: Reached his peak over hurdles when winning a valuable race at Leopardstown (2m, soft) last February but finished last in the County Hurdle here next time; the type to make a chaser and, after a laboured effort on his handicap chase debut at Naas, he fared better in a Down Royal novice in January; needs to show his jumping can hold up under pressure but this trip should suit better than the 2m he's been running over and plenty of potential remains.

runners.comment: Best on good ground, when 2m4f winner here last April; something to find on recent runs
runners.name: Theatre Native
runners.spotlight: Hurdle winner on heavy but best form on good ground, when a wide-margin winner of a mares' novice handicap chase on the New course (about 2m4f) last April; well held back here in November and at Leopardstown on Boxing Day which leaves her with something to find.

runners.comment: Has course form at 2m; creditable start for new yard but set a very different task here
runners.name: Western Zephyr
runners.spotlight: Useful 2m form for Charlie Longsdon in autumn 2024, including on this course, but his season ended badly; off to a good start for new yard when runner-up at Haydock (2m4f, soft; first-time cheekpieces, retained) last month but there's not much common ground between that run and what will be needed today.

runners.comment: Well treated on pick of course form; these very competitive races tend to be beyond him
runners.name: Grandeur dAme
runners.spotlight: Well treated on the pick of his Cheltenham form at about this trip, as when just touched off by Moon d'Orange last January, but he was pulled up last time out and these very competitive races tend to be beyond him.

runners.comment: Four chase wins at up to 2m4f but out of sorts since August, including for new yard latest
runners.name: Embittered
runners.spotlight: Four chase wins at up to about 2m4f on a range of surfaces but out of sorts since the latest of them, at Killarney in August, including for new yard on Friday; often wears cheekpieces, first-time blinkers now.

runners.breeder: Earl Elevage Marion & Mr Didier Marion
runners.comment: Won 2m4f chase here last January but pulled up at the Festival and below best since
runners.name: Moon dOrange
runners.spotlight: Pulled up in the 2m4f novice handicap here last March but that was out of character as he had won over that C&D the time before and generally has a good track record; not much of a force this season, though, and he doesn't look in enough form to take advantage of a weights drop; often wears headgear, first-time visor today.

runners.comment: 2m/2m1f wins last spring; just 3 runs since; much more is needed than Kempton 4th latest
runners.name: Yes Indeed
runners.spotlight: Won two in a row at Stratford and Newton Abbot last spring (2m/2m1f) for new yard; just three runs since, running respectably at Kempton last month following wind surgery, but so much more is needed at this level.

17:20.race_name: National Hunt Challenge Cup Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Could still have more to give, including with this stamina test and first-time headgear
runners.name: Wade Out
runners.spotlight: Switched to chasing with two wins in the autumn, the latter from One Big Bang in Listed race here (3m1f, soft) despite having been a detached last of the three remaining runners at the third-last fence; that was not a fluent round of jumping but, with a satisfactory Grade 2 run at Windsor in January under his belt, he could still have more to give, including with this stamina test and first-time headgear.

runners.comment: Sandown latest (3m, soft; won well from the front) confirmed he's got his act together
runners.name: Pic Roc
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten when just 17-2 at last year's Festival (2m4f); finally opened his chase account in November, before staying-on fifth in major handicap at Newbury (3m2f, good to soft) where he was badly hindered at the unsatisfactory start; 13l win at Sandown (3m, soft; made most) on latest outing confirmed he's got his act together, which earned a 7lb rise but he needs respect.

runners.comment: Up 10lb but now looks a prime candidate for serious stamina tests such as this if he jumps
runners.name: King Of Answers
runners.spotlight: Twice successful in small-field handicaps at Kelso (soft/heavy) over the extended 2m7f, easily on latest start (made most) despite the odd jumping indiscretion; wore first-time cheekpieces that day, in response to his Windsor run (3m, soft) in which he got going a good deal later even than the winner Guard The Moon; up 10lb since last time but he now looks a prime candidate for serious stamina tests such as this if his jumping holds up.

runners.comment: Ran well here when he had no answer to Wade Out late on in November (3m1f, soft)
runners.name: One Big Bang
runners.spotlight: Fifth in last year's Pertemps Final here as a staying hurdler and also ran well here when he had no answer to Wade Out after the final fence in November (3m1f, soft) on chase debut; readily beat a useful rival in a match at Southwell (3m, good to soft) next time and 2m3f offers an excuse for latest start, so he might be capable of better, which is needed.

runners.comment: Handicap debutant who is just a 5yo; promising runs at 2m7f and near 3m1f last two starts
runners.name: Kurasso Blue
runners.spotlight: 2-3 over hurdles and saw off useful opposition at Punchestown (2m7f, heavy) in December in his second chase; found one too good for him when 5-6 at Naas (near 3m1f, soft) two months ago but stuck to his task manfully; this handicap debutant is just a 5yo and the only one of that age to win this race in this last 100 years was in 1978, but this became a handicap only last year and he's trained by Gordon Elliott, so needs a close look.

runners.comment: 0-13 chasing; third in this last year off 5lb lower; beaten a neck over 3m6f in November
runners.name: Will Do
runners.spotlight: 0-13 now as a chaser but third in this race last year off 5lb lower; that was his best form last term and he's shown it only once since, when beaten a neck at Fairyhouse (3m6f, yielding to soft) in November; that was also his only long-distance assignment this term, so he could return to form with this step back up in trip; others are preferred for the win even so.

runners.comment: 2-3 as chaser; shaped latest (3m, soft; first cheekpieces) as if stamina was a strong suit
runners.name: Guard The Moon
runners.spotlight: Made a bad mistake at the fourth fence at Newbury in December and soon pulled up; clearcut winner of small-field novice handicaps at Aintree (2m4f, soft) and Windsor (3m, soft; first-time cheekpieces) in his other two chases and he shaped in the latter as if stamina was a strong suit.

runners.comment: Won the Grand National Trial at Haydock (extended 3m4f, good to soft) last time; up 6lb
runners.name: Grand Geste
runners.spotlight: Impressive in a useful handicap at Haydock (extended 3m1f, soft) and, following a Doncaster flop, even better when he emerged on top in the Grand National Trial back at Haydock (extended 3m4f, good to soft); up another 6lb but little to prove regarding stamina and should have more to give.

runners.comment: His breakthrough win was over an extended 2m5f but a Cheltenham 3m1f display augurs well
runners.name: Backmersackme
runners.spotlight: Made up a lot of ground when second in handicap at Cheltenham (3m1f, good) in October; disappointingly no show in a top 3m handicap at Leopardstown at Christmas but he took another valuable prize there (soft) five weeks ago; has a revised mark and that breakthrough win was over an extended 2m5f but the Cheltenham display augurs well, as do his connections.

runners.comment: Impressive last time but a move away from such testing ground looks the chief worry
runners.name: Holloway Queen
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 6yo mare seen mostly on soft or heavy, including for her three wins; unseated on chase debut but fourth at Newbury (2m6f, good) next time was satisfactory and she built on that in a major way at same track (extended 2m7f, heavy) one month ago, careering 14l clear late on; up 10lb and in trip, but a move away from such testing ground looks the chief worry.

runners.comment: Chase career began with a strong finish over an extended 3m1f; wins over shorter since
runners.name: Iceberg Theory
runners.spotlight: Bids for a hat-trick after scoring over an extended 2m6f at Limerick (good) in May and moving nearly 7l clear on the run-in over 2m5f at Cork (yielding) in November; the latter is easily his best form but his chase career began with a strong finish over an extended 3m1f last March, which sparks interest for this test.

runners.comment: A prime candidate, for last year's winning trainer, if the jumping mistakes can be avoided
runners.name: Newton Tornado
runners.spotlight: Got the fourth-last fence all wrong here in October and pulled up at Newbury after a mistake; there's a strikingly good side too, however, as he scored comfortably at Bangor (3m, heavy) and Doncaster (3m, soft) in his other two chases; looks sure to stay beyond 3m; up another 6lb but he's a prime candidate, for last year's winning trainer, if the mistakes can be avoided.

runners.comment: Work to do on a few counts, including after he didn't jump well here in December
runners.name: First Confession
runners.spotlight: Pulled up at 50-1 in last year's 3m Grade 1 novice hurdle here; ran well in three of his five chases this term, notably with his easy win in a 2m5f beginners' event at Carlisle (good to soft) last time, but Cheltenham in December was one of the exceptions and he didn't jump well that day, before falling at Exeter on his next start; work to do on a few counts.

runners.comment: Maiden; 0-8 in chases; runner-up in a 3m4f Dublin National but needs a big career best
runners.name: Union Station
runners.spotlight: Maiden; 0-8 in chases; runner-up in the Dublin National over 3m4f at Leopardstown last March and over 3m at the same track in December, both on yielding ground; 2m in cheekpieces did not work out last time; right back up in trip today but needs a big career best.

runners.comment: Sparked once last term; much more like it on latest start (3m) but stamina is big question
runners.name: Walking On Air
runners.spotlight: Easily best show last term came in the Great Yorkshire at Doncaster (3m, good; fell at the final fence) and finally back near that when third with first-time cheekpieces in same race (soft) this January on latest outing; dropped right out of it from home turn when just 7-1 for 3m2f Kim Muir here last March and pulled up lame in Scottish National, so stamina is a big question.

runners.comment: Competitive mark if bouncing back from latest start but going beyond 3m is something new
runners.name: Silver Thorn
runners.spotlight: Plenty to like about his wins in six-runner handicap chases (3m, good to soft) at Doncaster and Exeter; heavy ground might be the excuse when he was hammered by Holloway Queen at Newbury on latest start; has a competitive mark if back on song but going beyond 3m is something new.

runners.comment: Second over an extended 3m4f; progressive until he ran poorly at Haydock on latest outing
runners.name: Holokea
runners.spotlight: Won at Ffos Las (3m1f, soft) in October and runner-up in four of his other five chases, including when mown down late on in a big field at Windsor (extended 3m4f, soft) in January; progressive to that point but then ran poorly behind Grand Geste at Haydock on latest outing.

13:38.race_name: Fairlight Studios Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Sea Pigeon Series Qualifier)

runners.comment: Won latest hurdling start last May but winter AW form was very disappointing
runners.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners.spotlight: Won Bangor maiden (2m, good; first-time cheekpieces) on latest hurdling start last May and could plausibly have some improvement to come in handicap hurdles but this winter's AW form was very disappointing and she needs to prove her wellbeing.

runners.comment: Only 2lb higher than when making all over C&D in October and not yet fully exposed
runners.name: Captain Cool
runners.spotlight: Unseated rider recently but the form of his fourth in a higher-grade race at Musselburgh (1m7f, good to soft) in January reads well in this context, and he's only 2lb higher than when making all over C&D (good to firm) in October; not fully exposed, and can make bold bid in refitted cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Flopped badly last time but started off for Iain Jardine with three good runs (one win)
runners.name: Newport
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish 6yo who started off for Iain Jardine with three good runs in the autumn, the most notable a win at Musselburgh (1m7f, soft; also suited by good); flopped badly on latest outing but has possibilities if back on song after subsequent wind op.

runners.comment: Second on handicap hurdle debut in September; back over jumps after good AW win this year
runners.name: Cosmic Soul
runners.owner: M Lee D Lee C Jolley & Neville
runners.spotlight: Runner-up to a dual subsequent winner on handicap hurdle debut at Perth (2m, good) in September and reverts to this discipline after clearcut 2m AW win in January; could still have untapped potential over jumps; must be considered.

runners.comment: Flat form in second half of 2025 was uninspiring and he fell on his hurdle return
runners.name: Lahire
runners.spotlight: Won C&D juvenile hurdle in 2023 and is well handicapped on some of last season's placed efforts but his Flat form in second half of last year was mixed and he fell when back over hurdles in January; others have less to prove.

runners.comment: Pulled up over C&D last month and now 0-28 overall
runners.name: Warrior Lion
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in basement-grade AW race in January but pulled up over C&D (good to soft) when back over hurdles last month and now 0-28 overall; stable has much more obvious chance with Captain Cool.

runners.comment: Unexposed after only five hurdle runs but needs a good boost from the new blinkers
runners.name: Jet Approach

runners.name: War Memorial
runners.spotlight: A case can be made on 2025 best, including a C&D second last March, but he has finished out the back in four runs for new trainer this winter.

runners.comment: Improved to win 6f fillies' handicap last week; unexposed but needs more to defy penalty
runners.name: Ruby Red Gove
runners.owner: Alfa Site Services & Alan Gove Racing
runners.spotlight: Stepped up on her novice/maiden efforts when landing a fillies' handicap at Wolverhampton (6f) last week; had a bit more in hand than the neck margin suggests but she will still need a step forward to defy a penalty; after just four starts that is quite possible, however.

runners.comment: Three-time C&D winner; good third latest; stable enjoyed a productive February
runners.name: Jesse Luc
runners.spotlight: Won six times in the first half of 2025, three of them over C&D; close third at Kempton last time and he should go well for a stable who were in fine form in February (6-12).

runners.comment: 0-15 but he arrives on the back of two solid runs; better drawn today than last time
runners.name: Farandaway
runners.spotlight: Still seeking his first win after 15 attempts but he has run well in defeat on his last two starts, beaten under one length into fourth at Newcastle before a good C&D third 18 days ago; better drawn today and he holds each-way claims once again.

runners.comment: Lacks consistency but he's capable on his day; not ruled out from a handy draw
runners.name: Judgment Call
runners.owner: Paul Corrigan & Miss L A Perratt
runners.spotlight: Not the most consistent but still capable on his day, as when winning a 6f handicap at Newcastle in December (2lb higher today); handy draw and no surprise to see him show up well.

runners.comment: Four-time C&D winner; back to last winning mark and can't discount him
runners.name: Dark Side Thunder
runners.spotlight: Four of his nine wins have come over C&D; back to last winning mark and today's return to 0-70 company is in his favour; can't discount.

runners.comment: Ex-Irish 5yo; dropped back to 6f for stable debut; good apprentice booked; interesting
runners.name: Velvet Skies
runners.spotlight: Three wins in Ireland, including one over this trip on the AW at Dundalk; running creditably over further this year and he makes his stable debut back sprinting; promising 7lb claimer booked and new yard in good order; one to consider.

runners.comment: Good 3rd (5f) here in January; failed to build on it latest; up in trip with a hood added
runners.name: D Flawless
runners.spotlight: 1m winner for the Gosdens in May 2024; best effort for this yard came when a close third in a 5f handicap here in January; not so good at Newcastle last month; steps back up in trip with a hood fitted.

runners.comment: Conditions no problem but recent return to action was a low-key one and he's drawn widest
runners.name: One More Dream
runners.spotlight: Prolific AW winner, including C&D, but 3lb higher than for his last win; low-key return from a break here 18 days ago; best watched from the widest stall.

runners.comment: Infrequent winner but his C&D 2nd in December (off this mark) reads well; one to consider
runners.name: Dc Cogent
runners.owner: J R Dwyer And B Smart
runners.spotlight: His second to Supreme King over C&D in December has been franked since and he races off the same mark today; only sixth over C&D 18 days ago but that race wasn't run to suit; this could be more truly run and he's capable of a prominent showing.

runners.comment: 2yo promise not been matched in handicaps; returns from a break with a visor added
runners.name: Hi Lord
runners.spotlight: Second and first in two 2yo starts for Roger Fell; yet to shine in handicaps but he has dropped 12lb from his opening mark; returns from 132 days off with a visor added.

runners.comment: On a reduced mark but hit and miss for current yard; returning tongue-tie should help
runners.name: Brave Empire
runners.owner: James Paul Services To Industry Ltd
runners.spotlight: Now 24lb lower than for his stable debut last May; the odd promising effort on AW this winter but he needs to leave a low-key C&D run 18 days ago (wide draw) behind him; the returning tongue-tie can help.

runners.comment: 2nd in 4 of her 8 runs for E Walker; sold 5,000gns last month; still has time to come good
runners.name: Crystal Dagger
runners.spotlight: She finished second in four of her eight starts (6f-1m) for Ed Walker before changing hands for 5,000gns last month; still has time to do better and she is worth a market check starting out for her new stable.
